STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a square plate is typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a standard dinner-size square plate, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference cue: the chicken pieces are roughly 10-11 cm long (about one drumstick-length each), and the plate spans about 2.2-2.5 of those across its width. That gives roughly 24-27 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm (area 625 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Chicken (two thick pieces, skin-on, roughly 9 x 6 cm each, about 2.5 cm thick): footprint ≈ 2 x 54 cm² ≈ 108 cm² (about 17% of the plate). Thickness ~2.5 cm, so volume ≈ 270 ml x 1.0 = ~270 g. Chicken is fairly lean but fatty skin-on portions are present, so I estimate ~200 g of cooked chicken after accounting for the thinner edges.
- Mixed greens (bok choy / leafy greens, cooked, with stems): footprint ≈ 25% of plate ≈ 156 cm², average thickness ~2 cm (mound with stems) → ~312 ml x 0.6 = ~190 g.
- Mushrooms (about 5 whole, cooked, round, ~3 cm each, ~15 g each): ~5 x 15 g ≈ 75 g, with partial hidden pieces under greens, roughly 60-80 g.
- Cooking oil/juices, minor: ~5 g, ignored.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no rice or grain base is visible. The greens and chicken sit directly on the plate, so no additional hidden base is added. Total is a moderate single-serving meal, about 450 g.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (cooked):
- Chicken (skin-on, roasted/pan-fried): ~220 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked leafy greens (bok choy): ~15 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked mushrooms: ~25 kcal/100 g.

Energy estimate: chicken 200 g ≈ 440 kcal; greens 190 g ≈ 30 kcal; mushrooms 70 g ≈ 18 kcal. Total ≈ 490 kcal.
